{{Quote|This.. A key to one of the largest Massassi temples on this moon. I won't bore you with the details, but suffice it to say to say it holds great strategic value.|Alliance general Jan Dodonna, on the key contained in the Yavin Vassilika|<ref name="Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 5">[[Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 5|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'' 5]]</ref>}}
The '''Great Temple''', commonly referred to as the '''Massassi Temple''', was built on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] by the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] to worship [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] who had enslaved the Massassi. The Temple later housed the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] base, known as '''Massassi Base''', and the [[Jedi Praxeum]]. The Temple was [[Invasion of Yavin 4|destroyed]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] occupation of Yavin 4.

==History==
===Ancient history===
Around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> having [[Battle at the Denarii Nova|fled]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] after his [[Second battle of Korriban|defeat]] at the end of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] hid in the jungles of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] alongside his loyal [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] warriors called the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]]. They settled on a [[Massassi Site/Legends|site]]<ref name="FOTSE5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]]</ref> on the [[Ersham Ridge]]<ref name="Strongholds" /> covered with thick rainforests,<ref name="FOTSE5" /> and Sadow ordered his warriors to clear the area and start building moliminous monuments in his honor. Through [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemical]] experimentations, Sadow mutated the Massassi, turning them into [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]-wielding monsters.<ref name="darklords4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref>

In [[3997 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] arrived on Yavin 4 and took control of the Massassi descended from Naga Sadow's followers.<ref name="darklords4" /> He then ordered them to build temples for him to focus the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].<ref name="darklords5">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 5]]</ref> The Great Temple, a colossal ziggurat of [[Stone (disambiguation)|stone]],<ref name="dbGT">{{DB|location|massassitemple|Massassi Temple}}</ref> was one of these temples.<ref name="TSW6" />

During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], Exar Kun used the Great Temple as a base of operations. [[Tuk'ata/Legends|Tuk'ata]] inhabited the Great Temple during this time.<ref name="TSW4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 4]]</ref> At the [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Great Sith War)|end]] of the Great Sith War, Kun drained the Massassi in the Great Temple in order to survive as a [[Force ghost/Legends|ghost]].<ref name="TSW6" />

The Great Temple was so huge that it seemed impossible it could have been built without the aid of modern [[gravitonic construction]] techniques, yet all evidence pointed to mere hand technology and simple machines.<ref name="ANHN">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> How such an enormous structure was built was still a matter of speculation at the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The method that the Massassi used to cut and transport metric-ton monoliths from the crust of the moon without disturbing the surface remained a mystery to modern-day scientists.<ref name="GG2" />

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|I grow tired of asking this so it will be the last time: ''Where'' is the rebel base?|audio=WhereIsTheBase-ANH.flac|Grand Moff Tarkin to Princess Leia Organa|<ref name="SWE4" />}}
During the Galactic Civil War, [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] scout [[Dr'uun Unnh/Legends|Dr'uun Unnh]] discovered the temple.<ref name="Insider 92">{{InsiderCite|92|Refresher Reading}}</ref> The Alliance chose Yavin 4 due to its exclusion from official Imperial maps, [[1 BBY/Legends|after]] being forced to secretly abandon their former [[Dantooine base/Legends|base]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].<ref name="NEC" /> After retrieving the Temple's key from the [[Yavin Vassilika]], a fabled gem-like statuette,<ref name="Vas">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> Alliance generals [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and [[Roons Sewell]] were tasked with establishing the "Massassi Station"&mdash;also known as "Yavin Base," callsign "Base One"&mdash;within the Great Temple.<ref name="Empire">[[Empire 11|''Empire'' 11]]</ref> That same year, the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] security check-in [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]] heard of the base, and accidentally let slip of its existence before stopping himself.<ref name="STAC">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> However, despite the revelation of that imprudent droid, the Empire did not get wind of the base's location until one year later.<ref name="SWE4" />

Following its refit by the Alliance, the interior of the Great Temple had changed so much that its original Massassi builders would never have recognized it. The rock walls had been mostly replaced with metal, and poured paneling had been used to divide chambers instead of wood. The Rebels had also excavated new layers into the rock below the ziggurat to create a series of underground hangars linked by a turbolift platform. On the ground level and upper floors, many rooms had been converted for modern service, such as the [[Strategy Center|War Room]]. Only the [[Grand Audience Chamber]], a vast throne room located on the uppermost level of the Great Temple had been spared, for it had been deemed too beautiful and clean for the technicians to modify.<ref name="GG2" /> The proper maintenance of the new base required an abundance of staff, including a [[Janitor/Legends|janitor]] and several [[Deck officer/Legends|deck officers]], some of whom were barely kids at the time.<ref name="RF">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Force]]'' series</ref> Additionally, a section of the base was given over to refugees.<ref name="GG 1">{{WEGCite|story=Dodonna's Story|book=Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope|reprint=1}}</ref>

[[File:The_Final_Ship_BotF_Age_of_Rebeillon_by_Bradbury.png|thumb|left|250px|The Rebels are attacked by the Imperial forces]]
One year [[0 BBY/Legends|after]] the establishment of the Massassi Station,<ref name="NEC" /> the Rebel Alliance launched its assault on the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] from this facility. After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle]], the [[Royal Award Ceremony/Legends|Royal Award Ceremony]] was held in the Great Temple to honor the victors.<ref name="SWE4" /> However, the time of revelry proved to be short-lived. Six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the destruction of the Death Star over Yavin, the Rebel Alliance was forced to abandon the Great Temple. During the [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuation]], General Dodonna set off a series of concussion charges in the Temple. The sabotage knocked out a squadron of [[TIE/ca Punisher/Legends|TIE/IT Interdictor starfighters]] and the General was presumed killed.<ref name="NEC" />

In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] established his [[Jedi Praxeum]] in the temple.<ref name="DA" /> In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Admiral [[Natasi Daala]]'s [[United Warlord Fleets|fleet]] [[Assault on Yavin 4|attacked]] it.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> Later that same year, [[Kyle Katarn]] confronted, and after an intense battle in the underground portion of the Temple, [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Empire Reborn)|defeated]] the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Desann]] during the [[Empire Reborn]] assault.<ref name="JK:JO">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref> In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], [[Tavion Axmis]] commanded [[New Reborn|her Reborn]] to suck the [[Force energy]] out of the above-ground portion of the Temple.<ref name="JK:JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> The temple was partially demolished in [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]] during the [[Third Battle of Yavin]], but promptly reconstructed by a joint New Republic-Jedi effort throughout [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].<ref name="YJK:">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Under Siege]]''</ref>

The Temple was destroyed down to ground level<ref name="EOVI">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory I: Conquest]]''</ref> by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]],<ref name="ERC" /> although the underground levels remained partially intact.<ref name="EOVI" />

==Layout==
{{Quote|There's one place that we haven't touched, though&mdash;the Grand Audience Chamber at the top of the Temple. All of the instructors and students here agree that it is just too beautiful to change.|Luke Skywalker to [[Anakin Solo]]|<ref name="TGG">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: The Golden Globe]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ITW_Great_Temple.jpg|thumb|180px|Great Temple cutaway]]
Internally, the Great Temple was divided into four levels, each representing a step of the ziggurat&mdash;each level was thus larger in floor plan than the one above, but all were outfitted on broadly similar plans with small cells, chambers and corridors around a large central space.

When the Rebel Alliance set-up their base, the outer surface of the Massassi Temple was left as untouched as possible. Interior chambers, however, were roughly hewn by the Rebels prior to being filled in with chambers and a main central lift cluster. Rebel engineers also reinforced the temple's original stone floors with [[Ferrocrete/Legends|ferrocrete]]. The base was powered by a generating station composed of stolen [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] reactor components two kilometers from the temple.<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

[[File:Temple_Plan_large.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Floor plan of the temple]]

The topmost level, was almost entirely taken up by the Grand Audience Chamber, used as a ceremonial hall by the Alliance garrison and later employed by the Jedi Academy as a teaching space. Under the Alliance, the next level contained officers' quarters, and the base's security, communications and medical facilities, with the central room serving as a command center; the Jedi would later convert this level entirely to accommodation and storage. On the level below, the central chamber was outfitted by the Alliance as the War Room, later re-named as the Strategy Center by the Jedi: this was where the Alliance commanders coordinated the fighter attack on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. The surrounding rooms on this level, used as stores and technical workshops by the Alliance, were converted by the Jedi to meeting-rooms, communications and computing bays, and kitchens and dining halls.

[[File:Yavin_Base_Hangar.png|thumb|200px|The hangar bay of the Rebel base]]

The lowest level of the temple was used by the Rebels and the Jedi alike as a vast hangar bay to store starfighters and other vehicles; there was also a second hangar beneath, plus cellars and catacombs that remained largely unused in both phases of reoccupation. Access to the hangar was by a set of ground-level blast-doors, opening out onto a landing pad.

A viaduct was located near the Temple's entrance, along with an altar and a fountain with stone pillars. An overlook was available across a canyon.<ref name="BFI guide">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

During the Jedi period, the average ground level around the structure's exterior had risen, so that the main entrance was at War Room level, and many of the students thought of the entire hangar complex as being essentially underground - although the hangar doors must have remained accessible, the area in front of them no longer served as the main landing zone. The entrance faced a clearing, while a river now flowed close to the temple along the other two sides. Also during this time, a room known as the [[Hall of Judgment]] was built within the temple.

The Jedi divided some spaces into [[Sleeper (furniture)|sleeping]] and [[Refresher/Legends|refresher]] units for the students, and hanged heavy drapes above the [[Window/Legends|window]] holes. The original windows of the Temple had no [[Glass/Legends|glass]] because of Yavin 4's warm climate. However, heavy storms would arise every few months, and rain would whip through the jungle while the temperature dropped significantly. When that happened, the drapes kept the temple dry and warm.<ref name="TGG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-massassitemple.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Massassi Temple concept art by Ralph McQuarrie]]
The Great Temple was first seen in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the [[original trilogy]], which was released in [[1977]].<ref name="SWE4" />
The temple exterior was actually filmed in the ruins of the [[Wikipedia:Maya civilization|Mayan]] city of [[Tikal]], [[Wikipedia:Guatemala|Guatemala]]. A matte painting based on a concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] was also used to portray the front entrance of the Great Temple.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> This painting was enhanced digitally for the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] release of the film.<ref name="dbGT" />

In the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of ''A New Hope'', the "Mavassi outpost" was an Imperial installation located on Yavin. Princess Leia was imprisoned here, and [[Annikin Starkiller]] and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookee]] allies attempted to free her, but she had already been sent to the Imperial [[Death Star/Legends|space fortress]]. The building became the "Massassi Outpost" and a Rebel base in the second draft of the story.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
[[File:Great_Temple_Williamson.png|thumb|250px|[[Al Williamson]]'s early depiction of the Great Temple in [[Classic Star Wars 8|''Classic Star Wars'' 8]]]]
Throughout the history of the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], there have been many different depictions of the Great Temple. In the ''[[Classic Star Wars]]'' comic series, which was drawn by [[Al Williamson]], the Great Temple closely resembled some of the real monuments found on the site of Tikal, especially the shrine summit of the [[Wikipedia:Tikal Temple IV|Temple IV]], with only two levels and a rectangular base.<ref name="CSW">[[Classic Star Wars 8|''Classic Star Wars'' 8]]</ref> Later sources tend to portray the temple as a ziggurat&mdash;a terraced pyramid&mdash;but disagree on the global shape and number of levels. While both ''[[Galaxy Guide 2: Yavin and Bespin]]'' and ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' described the Great Temple as a pyramid with a square base and four levels, the video games ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''<ref name="SWGB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'' portrayed it as a truncated cone,<ref name="RS3">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> and ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' had it standing on an octogonal base.<ref name="IWSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> The [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 37|''Official Star Wars Fact File 37'']] stated that the temple had seven stories,<ref name="FF37">{{FactFile|37|YAV 5-6|Yavin 4 &ndash; Massassi Temples}}</ref> while ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' stated that it consisted of five distinct levels, plus an observation deck at the top.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|365|Great Temple, the}}</ref>

[[File:Great_Temple-SWGB_databank.png|thumb|left|Some sources portray the temple as a truncated cone.]]
In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' and in ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the station was depicted as being a small, grim-looking hangar with a control room in the back.<ref name="BFI">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref><ref name="BFII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> However, in ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', it was depicted as having a more elaborate interior, with hangars, training rooms, and the Grand Audience Chamber.<ref name="JK:JA" /> The [[2001]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' featured an alternate history scenario where Darth Vader attacks the Rebels on Yavin 4 in revenge for the Death Star. The player, flying in Vader's [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]], can fly into the Great Temple to attack the Rebel transports there. In ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', it was seen as containing a large hangar, and many rooms, including the room where Princess Leia and other Rebel leaders were stationed during the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="RS3" />
